title: A field guide to visual generation for XR

provenance.basis: Concise editorial summaries of the review framework, catalogue, and proposed evaluation agenda.
source_sections: Methods: Assets, Scenes, and Dynamic Worlds
XR Systems, Workflows, and Model Selection
provenance.resource_verification: All six selected resource titles, publication years, and source URLs were checked against their NeurIPS or CVF proceedings records on 23 October 2026.

axes.title: Content unit
axes.question: What does the application receive?
axes.explanation: Start with the unit exposed to the application: an object, an environment, prepared motion, or observations generated as actions arrive.
axes.reading_tip: Separate changes in viewpoint, changes over time, and changes caused by an action. They require different forms of retained information.

axes.title: Generative mechanism
axes.question: How is content constructed or updated?
axes.explanation: A pipeline may optimize a particular instance, sample a learned model, arrange existing assets, or generate observations and fuse them into geometry.
axes.reading_tip: Trace the full sequence of operators. Learned models, procedural rules, and explicit constraints can all contribute to one result.

axes.title: Representation
axes.question: What structure can the next component use?
axes.explanation: Distinguish the generator's internal state, the representation used for rendering, and the artifact delivered to the application.
axes.reading_tip: A point cloud used as a generation condition differs from geometry exposed for interaction. Check each conversion and the operations that survive it.

axes.title: Operating stage
axes.question: When does generation enter the user loop?
axes.explanation: Content can be prepared before viewing, rendered locally, replaced after asynchronous editing, or generated continuously from incoming context.
axes.reading_tip: Locate the first usable response. Generation speed, rendering rate, and input-to-display delay measure different stages of a system.

domains.title: Visual assets
domains.what: Objects and localized elements, from complete shapes to textured surfaces and separately represented parts.
domains.inputs: Text, images, multiview observations, supplied geometry, or random latent codes, depending on the method.
domains.outputs: Meshes, part collections, point clouds, fields, materials, and other renderable object representations.
domains.operations: Inspect the exposed editing unit. Placement, part manipulation, collision behavior, and saved edits each depend on the delivered structure and application components.

domains.title: Spatial scenes
domains.what: Arrangements and connected environments built through layout generation, asset assembly, completion, or spatial expansion.
domains.inputs: Language, images, camera poses, layouts, geometry, and existing scene observations.
domains.outputs: Object layouts, scene graphs, meshes, Gaussian scenes, or camera-conditioned views; some methods combine several of these.
domains.operations: Check viewpoint control, disocclusion, object addressability, and any collision proxy. A retained scene and a generated view expose different interfaces.

domains.title: Dynamic content & worlds
domains.what: Time-varying 3D content and observations that evolve with camera commands, user actions, or changing conditions.
domains.inputs: Text, images, video, time, camera trajectories, actions, and retained context, as supported by each configuration.
domains.outputs: Prepared 4D representations, multiview video, generated observation streams, or visual responses coupled to an external state system.
domains.operations: Distinguish animation playback from action response. Revisit tests examine recall; edit-and-return tests examine whether an accepted change survives absence.

domains.title: XR systems
domains.what: Complete authoring and presentation workflows that connect visual generators with tracked input, user interfaces, rendering, and displays.
domains.inputs: User requests, spatial context, tracked head or hand input, selected previews, and prepared content.
domains.outputs: Immersive authoring interfaces, manipulated scene content, stereoscopic imagery, and displayed responses in a specified device setup.
domains.operations: Identify which component implements loading, manipulation, registration, state storage, and display. Judge the operation in the configuration and task actually tested.

agenda.title: Binocular viewing under head motion
agenda.question: Does consistency measured offline predict viewing quality when the headset requests new left and right views?
agenda.design: Use the same content across applicable fixed-stereo, panoramic-rotation, and translated-view conditions. Record the renderer, stereo baseline, depth scale, display, and reprojection settings; vary presentation while retaining the content reference.
measurements: Cross-view geometric error and visible artifacts
Results separated by viewing condition and content dynamics

agenda.title: From preview to final asset
agenda.question: Which size, placement, and appearance decisions remain valid when a preview is replaced by final geometry?
agenda.design: Retain the preview, user operations, and final asset. Replay matched requests with the same final asset and delivery time while changing preview format. A separate live study can test the complete workflow, including any selected-preview conditioning.
measurements: Scale, contact, volume, or projected-outline agreement
Preserved placement constraints and revised decisions

agenda.title: Persistent changes & shared state
agenda.question: Does a supported, accepted change survive leaving and returning, and agree across observers?
agenda.design: Apply an edit supported by the interface, confirm its success, move out of view, and return by another route. Pair this with an unchanged-scene revisit. Vary absence and occlusion; where available, compare stored state with rendered observations and action outcomes.
measurements: Retention among successful updates and overall completion
Identity, pose, appearance, and action-relevant state

agenda.title: Response latency & scheduling
agenda.question: How long does a user wait for a meaningful response and for a result that supports the intended operation?
agenda.design: Timestamp input, queues, retrieval, generation, transfer, rendering, and display. Compare scheduling strategies with the input trace, model settings, hardware, and network fixed; track local head-motion rendering separately when it continues during generation.
measurements: Time to first meaningful response and usable final result
Average and tail delay, content age, and superseded requests
Visual quality and task completion alongside timing

agenda.title: Physical-space alignment
agenda.question: Do placement, scale, occlusion, and appearance constraints survive changes in viewpoint and the physical environment?
agenda.design: Generate and place a constrained asset, then revisit after viewpoint or environmental changes. Hold the asset fixed to isolate alignment effects; hold registration fixed to test generated geometry. Record whether spatial inputs are measured, inferred, or manually specified.
measurements: Support-relative placement and reference-relative scale error
Geometry and appearance under changing light and partial occlusion

benchmarks.name: Objaverse-XL
benchmarks.title: Objaverse-XL: A Universe of 10M+ 3D Objects
benchmarks.role: A large collection of 3D objects for learning shape, appearance, and novel-view generation. Filtering and rendering determine the actual training subset.

benchmarks.name: DL3DV-10K
benchmarks.title: DL3DV-10K: A Large-Scale Scene Dataset for Deep Learning-based 3D Vision
benchmarks.role: Real scene videos supporting novel-view synthesis and scene representation learning across varied capture conditions.

benchmarks.name: SCOPE
benchmarks.title: What Makes for a Good Stereoscopic Image?
benchmarks.role: Headset preference annotations for static stereoscopic images, connecting image distortions with perceived viewing quality.

benchmarks.name: VBench
benchmarks.title: VBench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
benchmarks.role: Dimension-specific video evaluation covering properties such as subject consistency, temporal flicker, motion smoothness, and spatial relationships.

benchmarks.name: WorldScore
benchmarks.title: WorldScore: A Unified Evaluation Benchmark for World Generation
benchmarks.role: Camera-trajectory-based next-scene tasks for comparing controllability, visual quality, and dynamics across world-generation approaches.

benchmarks.name: 4DWorldBench
benchmarks.title: 4DWorldBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for 3D/4D World Generation Models
benchmarks.role: Evaluation of perceptual quality, conditioning alignment, physical realism, and consistency for 3D/4D generation from multiple input modalities.

steps.description: Filter the catalogue by domain, inputs, and publication year.

steps.title: Check the evidence

steps.description: Choose resources for the property being measured.
